prompt:
Edit this APIShield application design into a much cleaner, more refined TABBED WORKSPACE. Preserve its light grey/white/cobalt design family and dark slate sidebar, but substantially replace the crowded composition. The attached screenshot is the anti-reference for density: DO NOT show graph, repair inspector, source diff and test evidence simultaneously. Produce a flat front-facing high-fidelity desktop application screenshot, 16:10 landscape.

Exact hierarchy: 180px dark slate sidebar with small APIShield wordmark and only Workspace, Runs, Settings navigation plus Help at bottom. Slim top bar with project selector Shipping API and subtle text Local workspace; absolutely NO user avatar or account control. In the main area, compact 28px heading Shipping API, one short line Endpoint migration · committed Python source. Top-right just one solid cobalt action Review repair and one small pale green badge Tests passed. No giant introductory headline, no breadcrumb stack, no metrics row, no large stepper, no marketing claims.

A BEAUTIFUL PROMINENT HORIZONTAL TAB BAR across the main content with exactly Overview / Impact graph / Code changes / Tests & rules. Impact graph selected. Tab labels have professional Lucide-style icons, measured spacing, a crisp cobalt underline and clearly contrasting selected text. Tabs are the central navigation affordance and should feel elegant and interactive. Only the selected tab's content appears.

Below this tab bar, ONE spacious white graph canvas occupies most of the main workspace, without nested white cards. A slim internal toolbar reads Impact graph and small secondary hint Select a node to inspect its evidence, with unobtrusive Fit view, minus, plus controls on the right. Four small beautifully crafted evidence nodes have room around them, arranged left to right across the central part of the canvas: API operation POST /labels (with short Endpoint moved marker), consuming function create_label with small src/parcel.py path, business rule Preserve exact grams, linked pytest test Shipping weight check. Connect them with thin, precise relation lines that represent observed API usage and declared rule/test links; labels are tiny secondary hints observed or declared. Colour is subtle: blue operation/function icons, amber rule icon and sage test icon. Nodes ~180px wide and 80px high, no glowing halos, enormous icons or long paragraphs. Small node selection affordance, no inspector OPEN on this screenshot. Graph details belong in an on-demand drawer in implementation. At bottom of canvas a compact legend Observed in code · Developer-declared and Graph / List toggle, nothing else. Avoid decorative grid backgrounds.

Below the canvas only a small quiet sentence Original code stays unchanged. Need guidance? Start the example. No extra panels, no source code, no diff, no test table, no cards of explanatory text. Those belong to their own tabs. Show ample breathing space and an excellent finished app component system: crisp typography, well-balanced headings, compact rounded buttons, subtle hover/selected affordances, clean 10px geometry and nuanced slate borders. Information must feel easy to understand at a glance, not packed. Use the reference's visual identity, improve its proportions. Add tiny Design concept label near Help so this isn't mistaken for a production screenshot. Do not invent transitive analysis, extra files, success percentages, timestamps or semantic-proof claims. A much simpler and nicer application with exactly one meaningful view in focus.
note: User prefers first concept light family, rejects crowded composition. Tabbed single-view revision. Graph arrow semantics must reflect actual consumes/scopes/checked_by edges rather than illustrative sequence.
